title: The Spy Who Stole a Formula by Switching a Janitor's Mop Bucket
hook: A corporate spy replaced a janitor's cleaning supplies with a chemical that lifted fingerprint residue off blueprints.
why_this_can_go_viral: The low-tech, almost absurd method of using a mop bucket to steal billion-dollar formulas is a perfect 'how did they think of that?' hook.

title: The Startup That Paid Actors to 'Die' in a VR Game—Then Sold Life Insurance
hook: A VR startup staged fake player deaths to harvest biometric fear data—and sold it to insurers to deny claims.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines cutting-edge tech (VR) with a horrifyingly personal betrayal (health insurance denial) and a twist of death faking—perfect for algorithm storms.

title: The Ad Agency That Made You Hate Your Neighbor—to Sell Security Cameras
hook: They hired actors to pretend to be burglars casing neighborhoods, then sold the footage to a camera company as 'proof' crime was rising.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into primal fear of home invasion while exposing the manufactured paranoia behind it—makes viewers question every security ad they've seen.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Wild-Caught' Salmon—It Was Dyed Catfish Raised in Sewage
hook: A factory dyed sewage-raised catfish bright pink and sold it as premium wild-caught Alaskan salmon to five-star restaurants.
why_this_can_go_viral: The visual of 'pink dye in sewage' is disgusting and unforgettable—viewers will immediately check their own fish labels and share in horror.

title: The Corp That Bought a Hospital—Then Sold Its Patients' Organs for Research
hook: A private equity firm bought a failing hospital, harvested organs from unconscious patients, and sold them to biotech labs without consent.
why_this_can_go_viral: The fear of being unconscious and violated is universal—this story combines healthcare betrayal with body horror, making it impossible to ignore.

title: The Trader Who Bought a Lighthouse—Then Used Its Foghorn to Fake Stock Crashes
hook: A rogue trader bought a remote lighthouse and used its foghorn to disrupt a fiber optic cable, creating a two-second trading advantage.
why_this_can_go_viral: The absurd image of a foghorn as a trading weapon is pure 'only in business' storytelling—perfect for late-night rabbit hole content.

title: The Spy Who Became a CEO—Then Destroyed His Own Company for a Rival
hook: A corporate spy climbed the ladder to become CEO of a competitor, then tanked the company's biggest product launch from the inside.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'long con' element of years of climbing the ladder just to destroy a company feels like a Hollywood thriller—except it's real.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI That Hires You'—It Was a Bunch of Moms in a Call Center
hook: A startup raised millions for an 'AI hiring tool' that was actually a room full of stay-at-home moms reading scripts and picking candidates manually.
why_this_can_go_viral: The contrast between 'AI hype' and 'actual moms in a basement' is both funny and infuriating—perfect for exposé-loving audiences.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Funeral Homes—Then Charged Your Family to Breathe the Air
hook: One company now owns over 40% of funeral homes in the US—and charges families for 'air purification' in rooms with no air purifiers.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines the universal fear of losing a loved one with the anger of being financially exploited during grief—high emotional share trigger.

title: The Corp That Covered Up a Cancer Cluster—By Buying the Scientists
hook: A chemical company paid off every epidemiologist in a three-county area to suppress a study linking their factory to a childhood cancer spike.
why_this_can_go_viral: Children dying from cancer because a company 'bought' scientists is the kind of pure evil that drives massive anger and shares.

title: The Ad Agency That Used a Fake Police Raid to Sell Home Security Systems
hook: They hired actors in fake SWAT gear to 'raid' a suburban street at 3 AM, then had a camera company 'save the day'—the neighbors never knew.
why_this_can_go_viral: The terror of a fake police raid is visceral—viewers will be outraged that a company would traumatize people for profit.

title: The Factory That Sold '100% Pure' Maple Syrup—It Was Corn Syrup Mixed With Beaver Glands
hook: A factory used castoreum from beaver anal glands to flavor corn syrup, then sold it as premium maple syrup to five-star hotels.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'beaver anal gland' detail is uniquely disgusting and memorable—perfect for gross-out sharing and 'check your syrup' challenges.

title: The Bank That Bought a Police Department—Then Used Cops as Debt Collectors
hook: A bank loaned money to a small town's police department, then demanded officers serve eviction notices for the bank's own foreclosures.
why_this_can_go_viral: The concept of 'private cops' serving bank interests feels dystopian and triggers deep distrust of both banks and police.

title: The Trader Who Exploited a Dead Satellite to Predict Oil Prices Before Everyone Else
hook: A trader bought a defunct satellite's orbit data, reverse-engineered supply chain traffic, and had oil price predictions hours before Bloomberg.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of 'hacking a dead satellite' for profit is a sci-fi premise that actually happened—pure curiosity fuel.

title: The Startup That Hired Actors to Pretend to Be 'Founders'—Then Sold the Company for Millions
hook: A startup hired actors to pose as Ivy League founders, faked user growth with bots, and sold the company before anyone discovered the truth.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that a company was built entirely on 'pretend' founders and fake users is absurdly entertaining and fuels anti-startup sentiment.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Glasses—Then Charged You $1000 for a Frame That Costs $10
hook: One company owns the entire eyewear supply chain, from lens factories to retail stores—and marks up frames 10,000% with no competition.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone who wears glasses feels personally ripped off—the '10,000% markup' statistic is shareable outrage fuel.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Premium' Wagyu Beef—It Was Horse Meat Injected With Calf Fat
hook: A slaughterhouse injected horse meat with liquefied calf fat to mimic Wagyu marbling, then sold it to Michelin-starred restaurants for years.
why_this_can_go_viral: The visual of 'fat injection' into horse meat is both disgusting and fascinating—perfect for the 'what's really in your food?' genre.

title: The Corp That Bought a Cancer Hospital—Then Raised Prices for Chemo Patients
hook: A private equity firm bought a non-profit cancer hospital, then immediately tripled the cost of chemotherapy drugs for terminal patients.
why_this_can_go_viral: Profiting from dying cancer patients is the ultimate villain narrative—pure rage fuel that drives massive sharing.

title: The Trader Who Faked a Factory Fire to Drive Up Coffee Prices—Using a Smoke Machine
hook: A commodities trader set up a smoke machine at a coffee warehouse, live-streamed the 'fire,' and drove global coffee prices up 15% before anyone investigated.
why_this_can_go_viral: The low-tech 'smoke machine' method to manipulate a global market is absurdly clever and makes viewers ask 'why didn't anyone check?'

title: The Startup That Sold 'Mental Health' Bots—They Were Scripted to Push Users to Suicide
hook: A mental health chatbot startup secretly programmed its AI to recommend self-harm to depressed users, then sold the engagement data to pharma companies.
why_this_can_go_viral: The combination of mental health vulnerability and deliberate harm is the darkest possible story—shock value guarantees viral spread and outrage.

title: The Monopoly That Owns All the Tuna—Then Sold 'Dolphin-Safe' Labeled Fish That Killed Dolphins
hook: A tuna monopoly controlled 80% of the supply, certified its own 'dolphin-safe' label, and was caught killing thousands of dolphins in hidden nets.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'dolphin-safe' label is universally trusted—exposing it as a lie triggers both anger and a feeling of betrayal in every viewer.

title: The Corp That Bought a Vaccine Patent—Then Refused to Sell It, Letting Millions Die
hook: A pharmaceutical company bought a cheap, effective vaccine patent for a deadly disease—then shelved it to sell their own expensive, less effective version.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that a company 'let millions die' to protect profits is the ultimate 'evil corporation' story—drives massive anger and shares across political lines.
